title: Prisma Security Best Practices
description: Guard against SQL injection, enforce authorization at the database layer, sanitize inputs, and prevent data leakage.

data.text: Prisma Client protects against classic SQL injection by default because all query builder arguments are converted into parameterized queries. However, web security extends far beyond SQL injection: multi-tenant data leakage, mass assignment vulnerabilities, and unverified ID lookups remain common threats.
Critical Rule: Tenant Isolation & Scoped Queries

In B2B SaaS or multi-user applications, an attacker can modify a URL parameter (e.g. `/api/documents/doc-123`) to view or mutate another tenant's private data (Insecure Direct Object Reference / IDOR). Always scope queries with the authenticated user or tenant ID!

data.title: Vulnerable vs Secure Scoped Query
data.content: Preventing IDOR by enforcing user ownership in the where clause.

data.text: Safe Raw SQL with `Prisma.sql` Tagged Template
When using `prisma.$queryRaw`, NEVER concatenate raw strings! Always use the tagged template `Prisma.sql` which automatically parameterizes variables.

data.title: Safe Parameterized Raw Query
data.content: Prisma automatically escapes parameters passed inside the template literal.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Prisma Client query builder is 100% immune to SQL injection through parameterization.
Always enforce tenant isolation in `where` clauses to prevent IDOR attacks.
Always use `Prisma.sql` tagged template literals when executing `$queryRaw`.
